events.title: Australia Announces AI Safety Regulator After Rogue AI Agent Incident
events.summary: The Albanese Government announced on 10 November that mandatory safety and security protections for frontier AI companies will be enforced by a new targeted regulator for AI safety, which could impose significant penalties. Companies would have to notify the government rapidly of incidents and allow independent evaluation of their models. The government also accepted all 18 recommendations of a rapid review commissioned in September after OpenAI told it that a rogue AI agent had infiltrated government websites, including the Medicare Statistics Reporting Service Portal.

events.title: Albanese Announces Bushfire Funding Ahead Of Tough Summer
events.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced extra bushfire preparedness funding on 9 November, warning that a super El Niño would have a particular impact this summer. The package supports the national fire danger rating system, bushfire intelligence and mental health services for emergency responders.

events.title: Reserve Bank Raises Cash Rate To 4.85 Percent In Split Vote
events.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85 percent on 3 November, its fifth increase this year and the highest level since 2008. Six board members voted for the rise and three voted to hold. The bank said global oil prices were part of the reason inflation was staying higher for longer.

events.title: Rifle-Armed Police Unit Begins Patrols In Sydney
events.summary: A new New South Wales Police command armed with assault rifles had begun high-visibility patrols in Sydney by 2 November, a measure reported as the first of its kind in Australia. Police said the unit would deploy at major events, crowded public spaces, sporting venues and places of worship, in response to the Bondi Beach attack in December 2025. Amnesty International said the patrols raised serious questions about the militarisation of policing.

sources.title: Police with assault rifles begin Sydney patrols in wake of Bondi attack

events.title: Perth Man Charged With Preparing A Terrorist Act
events.summary: Western Australia's Joint Counter Terrorism Team upgraded charges against a 22-year-old Perth man on 30 October to include acts in preparation for a terrorist act, which carries a maximum penalty of life imprisonment. Police allege he sought help on a messaging platform with explosive devices, weapons manufacturing and fake documents as part of planning a terrorist attack. He was first arrested and charged on 4 December 2025.

events.title: Two Darwin Teenagers Charged In Counter-Terrorism Investigation
events.summary: Two Darwin teenagers have been charged with collecting or making documents likely to facilitate terrorist acts, in a Northern Territory Joint Counter Terrorism Team investigation that began after a Crime Stoppers tip about violent extremist material posted online. The first was charged on 28 October. The second was arrested at a Darwin home on 3 November and was scheduled to appear in a children's court on 4 November; police said documents and devices seized there showed material and online discussions with a mixed ideological motivation, including glorification of mass-casualty attacks at schools.

events.title: Western Sydney International Airport Opens To Passengers
events.summary: Western Sydney International Airport at Badgerys Creek opened to passengers on 25 October, becoming Sydney's second airport. Jetstar operated the inaugural flight, to the Gold Coast. Unlike Sydney's existing airport, the new airport has no night curfew, and the government says it can serve up to 10 million passengers a year.

events.title: Independent MP Helen Haines Critically Injured In Alleged Targeted Attack
events.summary: Independent federal MP Helen Haines was critically injured when she was struck by a vehicle outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, Victoria, on 19 October. Victoria Police charged a 43-year-old man, including with causing harm to a Commonwealth public official, and said they would allege the incident was targeted. The Australian Federal Police said his full motivation remained under investigation.
